title: Business Date Features
description:
Acme’s POS dump stores event times as strings. Weekend dashboards and lag reports need calendar fields derived in Spark — not re-parsed in every BI query.

Read the input Parquet, append date features on every row, and write Parquet with overwrite. Keep every input column unchanged; only add the derived columns.

Derive in order: (1) `business_date` = calendar date of `event_ts` via `to_date`, (2) `sale_year` / `sale_month` from that date, (3) `day_of_week` using Spark `dayofweek` (1 = Sunday … 7 = Saturday), (4) `is_weekend` true when `day_of_week` is 1 or 7, (5) `days_to_as_of` = `datediff(as_of, business_date)` where `as_of` comes from the job env `BUSINESS_DATE` (platform sets `2024-06-15`).

Input columns: `txn_id`, `store_id`, `product_id`, `event_ts` (string `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss`). Implement with Spark DataFrame / `pyspark.sql.functions` — no Python date loops over collected rows. **Run** uses two smoke testcases; **Submit** uses the full set and row-diffs your Parquet against each case’s `expected/`.

Write results with `df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(OUTPUT_PATH)`. `OUTPUT_PATH` is set by the platform for **this Run/Submit only**.

problemStatement.overview: Append business_date, sale_year, sale_month, day_of_week, is_weekend, and days_to_as_of from event_ts; write Parquet to OUTPUT_PATH.
symptoms: Weekend vs weekday dashboards re-parse event_ts in every query.
Lag reports need a stable days-to-as-of column vs the job BUSINESS_DATE.
yourTaskSteps: Read input Parquet from INPUT_PATH (platform stages selected testcase inputs).
Append the six date-feature columns using Spark date functions and BUSINESS_DATE.
Preserve txn_id, store_id, product_id, event_ts; write Parquet to OUTPUT_PATH with overwrite.
Submit is graded with a row-level compare against each selected testcase expected/.
problemStatement.yourTask: Implement src/main.py that derives calendar features from event_ts and writes Parquet output.
hints: to_date(col("event_ts")) yields the calendar DATE used by year/month/dayofweek.
Spark dayofweek: 1 = Sunday … 7 = Saturday — document it; don’t assume ISO Monday=1.
spark.read.parquet(INPUT_PATH) reads every staged testcase file.

gradeChecks: Spark job succeeds on selected Submit testcases
OUTPUT_PATH Parquet readable with input columns plus the six date features
Each Submit testcase expected/ matches candidate rows (key + values)
No extra rows beyond the union of selected expected testcases
